3. neca-red-queen-11.jpg — complementary side/rear view of the long swept-back head crest, back, legs and articulated tail.
Use these three photographs only as visual references for the SAME RED creature. Reconstruct a strict right-facing side view; do not copy their three-quarter camera views.

Identity invariants in ALL four cells: the same distinctive very long backward-sloping red head crest, the same red ridged and layered carapace, tall ribbed neck and thorax, EXACTLY FOUR ARMS (two large primary arms and two smaller secondary arms below them), exactly two digitigrade legs, the same ivory teeth and pale facial horns/tendrils, the same long red segmented vertebral tail with its whole pointed tip. Living-creature rendering: detailed dark biomechanical horror game art, deep blood-red and burgundy chitin with dark recessed ribs and restrained natural wet highlights; preserve the red-reference identity and ivory facial details. Translate the photographed figure into living anatomy. No toy pivot holes, screws, ball joints, molded seam gaps or plastic display supports. No added orange glow, fire, magic or projectile.

Camera and registration: strictly 90-degree right-facing side profile in EVERY cell, fixed orthographic game camera, no change of view, no zoom. Use one identical anatomical stature, skull size, torso length, pelvis size and limb lengths across all four poses. Both planted feet must remain on precisely the same invisible local ground line and at the same local positions in every cell. Preserve pelvis/body registration; the requested changes are small upper-body animation poses, not walking or size changes. Clearly separate the silhouettes of the four hands enough that the two primary and two secondary arms remain identifiable in profile.

Cell order, left to right, top to bottom:
TOP LEFT — Rest 0: neutral alert standing posture, primary arms comfortably bent forward, secondary arms relaxed under the thorax, mouth mostly closed with ivory teeth visible, feet planted.
TOP RIGHT — Rest 1: the same rest pose with only a very subtle breathing/neck and finger change. Exactly the same planted stance and anatomical proportions.
BOTTOM LEFT — Early anticipation: grounded early attack windup; the head/neck begins to draw back slightly and the primary arms begin to prepare, with the smaller arms flexing close to the thorax. Feet and pelvis stay registered.
BOTTOM RIGHT — Advanced anticipation: a clearly later but still restrained windup, the same head and four arms visibly poised to act; the mouth may open slightly. This remains preparation only: no strike completed, no spit, no beam, no projectile, no effect, no victim.

Framing: four equally sized square cells. Each cell contains ONE entire creature including the complete crest, all hands, both feet and the entire tail. Keep generous visible transparent margins on every side, at least roughly 8 percent of the cell; the feet sit near 88 percent of the local cell height. Fit the complete curved tail behind the creature within that same cell, with a fully visible tip. No pixel of a creature should touch a cell boundary or overlap a neighboring cell. Keep the local ground line identical across the rows. Do not draw the ground line.

Output: clean isolated transparent cutouts only, identical lighting in all cells, no background color, no checkerboard drawn into the pixels, no scenery, no cast shadow on a floor, no captions, no numbers, no grid lines, no borders, no watermark. Requested sheet size is 2048 x 2048; preserve genuine alpha.

v1.definition: Pixels more than3source pixels from the alpha128 core; a diagnostic, not a semantic silhouette segmentation.

v2.definition: Pixels more than3source pixels from the alpha128 core; a diagnostic, not a semantic silhouette segmentation.

v1PixelComparison.statement: The built-in edit may re-render foreground detail; exact foreground pixel preservation is not claimed.

registration.coordinateConvention: Cell-local source pixels; body pivot at native center of ground contact. Arm scale is world pixels per source pixel at native actor height210, then multiplied by actor.h/210, not by bodyScale.
registration.layerMirror: One overall mirror preserves far-body-near layer order.
registration.uncertainty: Attachment and support coordinates are visual engineering measurements, not exact canonical anatomy. Narrow antialiased fringes remain; no software alpha threshold or resampling was applied to source PNGs.
registration.deathAlpha: Native globalAlpha0.3 is applied to each of five components; overlapping components can accumulate opacity. No offscreen group-opacity substitution.

integration.salvoCue: Private WeakMap marker only after new owned projectiles that are not held by the native outer insertion-grace owner. Native update advances and expires it before AI early returns; draw only reads.
integration.insertionGrace: The outer insertion-safe-zone mixin can truncate new projectiles in its finally block. A matching insertionGraceEnemyV188 owner prevents a false visual shot; the native four-second protection and projectile rules are unchanged.
integration.resume: Successful resume creates a new owner without replay; rejected resume retains old actor and cue.
integration.loading: Three exact same-origin PNG sources admitted atomically. Entry and successful resume may load/retry; drawing and late image callbacks cannot change actor state.
integration.culling: Conservative full-cell union of bodies and arms across poses and mirrors, only for the current ready owner. No physical collision expansion.
